Movement I · Day 1

From Prompt to Portfolio

First half-day · about 3 hours (proposed)
  1. AI tools overview

    AI tools for coding, design and productivity, plus reference UI websites. How to prompt AI to generate and refine web interfaces.

  2. UI recreation challenge

    Recreate or improve a given website design with AI tools. Focus on layout, typography, colours, responsiveness and interactions.

  3. Digital portfolio

    Build a personal portfolio that shows your projects and skills. Follow the reference or make your own version.

Timed challenge. Winners are chosen on the best web development outcome. The best implementations are showcased.
An example prompt Build a responsive portfolio page. Dark theme, serif headings, a hero with my name, three project cards and smooth hover effects. Make it work well on a phone.

Outcome

A working portfolio prototype and practical experience turning prompts into interfaces. The Day 1 Handbook in your resources walks you from zero to a finished page.

Movement II · Day 2

From Chatbot to Agent

About 2 hours (proposed)
Trigger
AI
Decision
Action
  1. AI chatbots vs AI agents

    What makes an agent different from a chatbot: models, tools, triggers, workflows and actions, with practical examples.

  2. Live workflow demonstration

    A visual automation tool such as n8n shows a simple trigger, AI, decision, action workflow. If feasible, a basic website or form connects to it, so one input gives a real, visible result.

  3. Mini experiment

    Modify a prepared workflow or prompt and test how different inputs change the output. See how validation and predefined rules control actions.

An example workflow trigger a student submits a form ai reads it and tags the topic decide urgent? yes: alert, no: queue action send a reply, save the record

Outcome

You understand the basic architecture of an AI-powered workflow and how its components connect. Modules 1 to 5 in your resources go deeper.

The ensemble

What makes an agent?

Five parts play together. Take one away and the music stops.

TriggersThe event that starts a run: a form, a message, a schedule.
ModelsThe AI that reads the input and decides what it means.
WorkflowsThe steps and rules that route work from start to finish.
ToolsWhat the agent can use: search, forms, apps and data.
ActionsWhat finally happens: send, save, update or reply.

Movement III · Day 3

Conduct Your Own AI Agent

Full day (proposed)
1
Problem and team formation

A practical problem is introduced. Teams form, pick a manageable solution and define the user, the workflow and the outcome.

2
Build the prototype

Create a simple web interface with AI-assisted development and an agentic workflow from a prepared tool or template. Use simulated data where live integrations are unavailable.

3
Test and improve

Test the whole user journey, fix workflow errors, improve the interface and prepare a short live demo.

4
Final showcase

Present your problem, solution and working prototype in a short live demonstration.

In every demo, show

What the AI does
What the workflow executes
What remains simulated

Judging is optional and subject to club approval.
